slides.title: Conditioning restricts the population; it does not imply time or causation

All outcomes
Evidence B
A ∩ B
P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B)
QUESTION
P(sick | cough)

Among people who cough, what fraction are sick?

REVERSE
P(cough | sick)

Among people who are sick, what fraction cough?

INTERPRETATION
“Given B” need not mean B happened earlier or caused A. Reversing the conditional changes the reference population.

slides.title: One observation can support several hidden causes
slides.visibleText:
Observed evidence can discriminate between competing causes.
OBSERVED NOW
Bad traffic

The vehicle slows because traffic is congested.

COMPETING HYPOTHESES
Construction or accident

Either hidden cause could explain the same observation.

DISCRIMINATING EVIDENCE
Barrels or flashing lights

Additional observations can shift belief between explanations.

INFERENCE TASK
Compare posterior beliefs after evidence—not merely which story sounds plausible.

slides.title: Two factorizations of the same joint yield Bayes' rule
slides.visibleText:
Thomas Bayes (1701–1761)
P(x,y) = P(x | y)P(y)
P(x,y) = P(y | x)P(x)

Set the two factorizations equal:

P(x | y)P(y) = P(y | x)P(x)

Divide by P(y), provided P(y) > 0:

BAYES' RULE
P(x | y) = P(y | x)P(x) / P(y)

slides.title: Posterior disease probability is not the probability that disease causes a symptom
slides.visibleText:
Disease

hypothesis d
causal direction →
Symptom

evidence s
← inferential direction
P(d | s) = P(s | d)P(d) / P(s)
POSTERIOR
P(disease | symptom)

Belief in disease after observing the symptom.

LIKELIHOOD
P(symptom | disease)

How probable the symptom is if the disease is present.

PRIOR
P(disease)

Belief before the current symptom is observed.

MEANING CORRECTION
Bayes' rule reverses a conditional; it does not prove causation.

slides.visibleText:

H₂
H₃
E = (E∩H₁) ∪ (E∩H₂) ∪ ··· ∪ (E∩Hₙ)
P(E) = Σᵢ P(E∩Hᵢ)
TOTAL PROBABILITY
P(E) = Σᵢ P(E | Hᵢ)P(Hᵢ)
WHY ADDITION WORKS
The hypotheses are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive, so the pieces are disjoint. No overlap subtraction is needed.

Distinguish event from variable, posterior from likelihood, association from cause, and MAP from ML.
